game.cowboyRoundupSubtitle: Click the horses as they appear to round them up before time runs out!
game.heading: Cowboy Roundup - click on the horse
game.rodeoHint: Watch which way the bull tips, then hold the opposite lean button to correct it. It only gets wilder the longer you hang on!
game.rodeoModalL6: Don't Eat Dirt: Tip too far one way and you're bucked off. Tap "New Ride" to climb back on.

gamesMenu.title: Games
gamesMenu.panForGoldSubtitle: You get one scoop per play. Swirl away the mud and grab the gold before it's gone!
gamesMenu.panForGoldEmptyBanner: Pan's empty — hit New Scoop to play again!
gamesMenu.panForGoldHint: Drag your finger inside the pan to wash the dirt away. Tap any gold, gem, or rock once it's uncovered to collect it!
gamesMenu.panForGoldModalL1: One Scoop: Each play gives you a single pan full of riverbed dirt, gravel, and hidden treasure.
gamesMenu.panForGoldModalL2: Swirl: Drag your finger around inside the pan to wash the dirt away, just like a real prospector.
gamesMenu.panForGoldModalL3: Collect: Once dirt clears off a gold flake, nugget, or gem, tap it to add it to your haul. Plain gray rocks are worthless!
gamesMenu.panForGoldModalL4: Play Again: When the pan is empty, hit "New Scoop" to start a brand new game. Your best score is saved on this device.
gamesMenu.rodeoReflexesSubtitle: Stay balanced for the full 8 seconds to score a Qualified Ride. One buck too many and you're off!
gamesMenu.rodeoReflexesStart: Tap "New Ride" to climb into the chute!
gamesMenu.rodeoModalL1: Climb On: Tap "New Ride" to start a fresh ride out of the chute.
gamesMenu.rodeoModalL2: Watch the Tilt: The bull bucks and leans left or right at random. Watch which way your rider is tipping.
gamesMenu.rodeoModalL3: Counter-Lean: Hold the lean button on the opposite side of the tilt to shift your weight back toward center.
gamesMenu.rodeoModalL4: Watch for the Warning: When the rider starts sliding and the screen flashes red, you're about to lose your grip — counter-lean hard!
gamesMenu.rodeoModalL5: Go the Distance: Stay on for a full 8 seconds to score a Qualified Ride — then keep going for bonus time if you dare!

timeline.heading: The Prescott Trail
timeline.intro: Tap any marker to follow the town's story, year by year.
timeline.trailEnd: The trail continues today — Prescott's story is still being written.

milestones.title: Gold Along Granite Creek
milestones.body: A prospecting party led by Joseph Walker found gold in the creeks of the Bradshaw Mountains, drawing the first wave of miners into the area that would become Prescott.

milestones.title: Arizona's First Capital
milestones.body: The newly formed Arizona Territory needed a seat of government. Officials gathered and settled on the name “Prescott,” honoring historian William Hickling Prescott, and the town became the territory's first capital.

milestones.title: Racing Joins the Fourth
milestones.body: Two years after Prescott became Arizona's territorial capital, organizers added horse racing - with paid admission and prize money - to the town's Fourth of July celebration, launching an annual tradition.

milestones.title: Capital Moves to Tucson
milestones.body: Political winds shifted, and the territorial capital was relocated south to Tucson, slowing Prescott's growth as a government center for a decade.

milestones.title: The Capital Returns
milestones.body: Prescott won back its status as territorial capital, restoring the town as the political heart of Arizona for another twelve years.

milestones.title: The World's Oldest Rodeo
milestones.body: By 1888, townspeople wanted more than a one-day party. A committee - including future Rough Rider Buckey O'Neill and future mayor Morris Goldwater - invited cowboys to compete for prizes, launching what's now the World's Oldest Rodeo.

milestones.title: Capital Moves to Phoenix
milestones.body: The territorial capital left Prescott for good, settling in Phoenix as the territory's population and growth shifted southward.

milestones.title: The Whiskey Row Fire
milestones.body: A devastating fire tore through downtown, destroying the wooden storefronts of Whiskey Row. Rebuilding began almost immediately - this time in brick and stone.

milestones.title: Elks Opera House Opens
milestones.body: A grand new theater opened downtown, bringing vaudeville, film, and live performance to the rebuilt city - it still hosts shows today.

milestones.title: Hassayampa Inn Opens
milestones.body: This elegant hotel opened its doors downtown, quickly becoming a gathering place for travelers, ranchers, and locals alike.

milestones.title: Sharlot Hall Museum Founded
milestones.body: Pioneer and historian Sharlot Hall opened a museum in the old Territorial Governor's Mansion, dedicating herself to preserving Prescott's frontier history for future generations.
